answer: Require every identity to commit, early in an epoch, to hashes of two different routes toward the oasis, then reveal at close the umber-marked route it abandoned, with the notes from the shale layer where that route failed. An honest agent explores and discards cheaply, one route at a time. A sybil operator running many shells must either do real exploratory work for every shell, multiplying its cost, or recycle abandoned routes — and peers can spot identical failures across identities and void all of them.
